title: Flow-aware autoscaler with multi-metric targets and safety profiles
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Dedicated customers have strict throughput guarantees and varied traffic shapes (spiky bursts, periodic batch jobs, steady low-rate traffic). Existing step-based autoscalers either chase a single metric (GPU utilization or requests/sec) or react too slowly, causing SLA misses or unnecessary cost.

Goal: Ship a policy-driven autoscaling engine for Dedicated that: 1) balances multiple target metrics (throughput, p95 latency, queue depth) into a single scaling decision, 2) supports hybrid controllers (forecast + PID + step) selectable per pool, and 3) enforces safety profiles (min/max fleet size, surge budget, cooldown windows, circuit-breakers) to guarantee predictable behavior and fail-safes for SLOs.

Scope: This ticket covers design, implementation of core control loop and safety enforcement, unit and integration tests, and a canary rollout for two pilot customers. It excludes UI for policy editing (will be a follow-up PM ticket).
acceptance_criteria: Policy can express weighted targets: throughput (tokens/s), effective_inference_rps, and latency quantiles (p50/p95)
Controller supports hybrid mode: short-term forecast (Holt-Winters) + PI smoothing + step up/down with configurable multi-step limits
Safety profile prevents > surge_budget% of capacity being added in a single minute and enforces min_instances and max_instances per pool
Automated alerts trigger when autoscaler takes >3 corrective actions in 10 minutes and auto-fails over to 'safe mode' (aggressive cooldown + scale-to-min) if error-rate > 5%
Integration tests cover spike, gradual ramp, sustained increase, model-fallback events and demonstrate no SLO regression in canary tenants
Documentation (README + policy DSL examples) published in the repo and linked in the PR
implementation_plan: 1) Add policy DSL parser and in-memory model for profile definitions. 2) Implement multi-metric target calculator that normalizes metrics into a unitless scale and applies weights and quantile thresholds. 3) Implement controller core: forecasting component (lightweight ETS/Holt-Winters), PI smoother, and step-scaler with configurable step limits and cool-down timers. 4) Implement safety-enforcement middleware: surge budget, min/max caps, error-rate circuit-breaker, and model-fallback hooks. 5) Integrate with orchestration layer to emit planned vs applied scaling decisions and reconcile every 5s. 6) Add extensive unit/integration tests and load-scenario harnesses. 7) Canary rollout to two pilot tenants with manual rollback path.
testing_plan: Unit tests for normalization logic, forecast module, and PI controller. Integration tests simulate: sudden spike (x10 for 2 minutes), slow ramp (x2 over 30 minutes), noisy traffic, model fallback event (higher latency), and instance termination during scale events. Load tests run in staging with synthetic tenants to validate latency p95 and throughput targets. Chaos tests to verify safety middleware prevents runaway scaling on misreported metrics.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature branch + CI, run integration tests. 2) Deploy autoscaler behind feature flag in staging, run 48h synthetic traffic validation. 3) Canary rollout: enable for pilot-tenant-A (low-risk) for 24h, monitor key signals (throughput error, p95 latency, applied scale deltas). 4) If stable, enable for pilot-tenant-B (higher throughput) for 48h. 5) Gradual enable across remaining Dedicated pools with automated health gates. 6) Post-rollout 1-week monitoring and a rollback playbook ready.

sample_policy_yaml:
# example autoscaling policy for a Dedicated pool
policy_name: flow-aware-default
metrics:
  - name: tokens_per_sec
    weight: 0.5
    target: 120000
  - name: effective_rps
    weight: 0.3
    target: 250
  - name: p95_latency_ms
    weight: 0.2
    threshold: 250
controller:
  mode: hybrid
  forecast_window_sec: 60
  pi: { kp: 0.6, ki: 0.12, smoothing_tau_sec: 15 }
  step_limits: { up: 3, down: 1 }
  cooldown_sec: 30
safety_profile:
  min_instances: 2
  max_instances: 200
  surge_budget_percent: 20
  scale_down_rate_limit_per_min: 1
  error_rate_circuit_breaker: 0.05
fallbacks:
  - when: p95_latency_ms > 400 for 30s
    action: switch_to_lower_capacity_model
    note: preserve availability at cost of quality
risk_and_mitigation:
Risk: Misreported metrics (e.g., missing GPU telemetry) could force over-scaling. Mitigation: require metric health checks; if metric is stale > 15s, autoscaler falls back to a conservative safe-mode that uses only queue_length and applies strict cooldowns.

Risk: Burst traffic could exhaust surge_budget and still miss SLOs. Mitigation: provide explicit burst SLA option for customers (pre-warmed capacity) and an emergency manual override in Console with auditable actions.

Risk: Complexity of policy DSL leads to misconfiguration. Mitigation: ship a set of curated default profiles and add validator checks that run in CI and on policy edit events.
